summary.headline: Rolex Rings Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4.3% to INR304 crore on labour-constrained output, while EBITDA margin expanded to 22.6% and PAT grew 22% to INR60 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR304 crore, up 4.3% YoY, which management said was short of its guided growth because a shop-floor labour shortage in April to mid-June limited output, not demand. Auto components grew 13.5% to INR163 crore while bearing rings fell 6% to INR118 crore, with softness concentrated in domestic and European industrial bearing rings. EBITDA was INR69 crore at a 22.6% margin (up 100 bps YoY) and PAT rose 22% to INR60 crore, the third straight quarter of YoY margin expansion. Management said operations normalised from June, July 2026 was the highest-revenue month since inception, and it reiterated mid-teen FY27 revenue growth guidance while cutting its margin guidance to 21-22% citing ocean freight costs.

segments.name: Auto components
segments.commentary: INR163 crore in Q1, up 13.5% YoY; about 72% exports. Export auto components INR118 crore, up about 30% YoY, while domestic auto components fell to INR45 crore from INR53 crore due to OEM production deferrals.

segments.name: Bearing rings
segments.commentary: INR118 crore, down 6% YoY; about 27% exports. Softness concentrated in domestic and European industrial and large-size rings, with export bearing rings down to INR32 crore from INR35 crore.

segments.name: Others (scrap)
segments.commentary: Management said the roughly 8% 'others' share of the revenue mix is scrap revenue; scrap was about INR20 crore in Q1 FY26 per the call.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance kept at mid-teens; management said FY28 could be more than mid-teens or close to 20%.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided conservatively at 21-22%, below the 22.6% in Q1, citing ocean freight up 2-3x; management flagged a 50 bps uplift in FY28 as possible.
FY27 capex guided at INR30-40 crore per year.
Utilisation at 63-65% currently, targeted at 70-72% by year end.
FY27 export auto components expected at INR425-450 crore (management ruled out INR500 crore); FY26 export auto components were INR350 crore.
Q2 FY27 expected to show better order book conversion now that labour is normalised; US customer volumes recovering from a 35-40% FY26 decline.
capex_capacity: Utilisation at 63-65%, targeted at 70-72% for FY27.
FY27 capex INR30-40 crore per year (annual basis).
One or two new plants of a key export customer expected to start supply in Q3 FY27; new orders also expected to start in Q3.
Capacity is fungible between bearing rings and auto components, per management.
Defence and aerospace: initial registrations and approvals obtained; defence revenue possibly within about 12 months.
demand_pricing: Export customers returning with orders after FY26 wait-and-see behaviour on tariffs; management said no customer was lost.
Allison revenue annualising near the FY25 level, per management; Dana initial development dialogues started with 12-18 months to revenue impact.
Domestic automotive bearing ring demand reported as improving, with customers increasing wallet share; industrial bearing ring guidance is marginal growth for the next couple of quarters.
Contract pricing is pass-through only for raw material and forex, not for value-add, so freight and fuel inflation cannot be fully recovered.
Ocean freight is 2-3x normal; some customers have agreed to reimburse, and one has changed import delivery terms.

qa_highlights.question: What was the labour shortage reason and was lost revenue deferred or lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited hot summer, vacations, weddings and crop season leave for semi-skilled workers; it said nothing was lost, output was deferred by about a month, and the fix is 3 shifts, overtime and temporary labour for 2-2.5 months at some extra cost.

qa_highlights.question: Will Rolex reach INR500 crore in export auto components in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said not INR500 crore but confident of INR425-450 crore, against FY26 exports of INR350 crore; the analyst noted Q1 annualises to about INR450 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin should be expected, and is 22% possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided conservatively to 21-22% for FY27 because of freight costs, and said a 50 bps uplift is possible in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US duty refund recognised in revenue or other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Some marginal US duty drawback refund was received in Q1 and is included in the numbers; management said refunds will be booked in revenue, not other income, and the major chunk is still pending.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash be deployed given the debt-free balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it may pay dividends or do another buyback after the INR180 crore buyback, and is exploring a JV with an overseas partner (global agency appointed, 6-9 months to outcome) and inorganic options.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic and Timken-linked bearing ring business decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the bearing ring export decline mainly to Timken's reduced business, and said it is diversifying to new customers in the US and Europe; no meaningful share recovery yet, with results expected in a couple of quarters.

risks_watch: Ocean freight and container availability: freight is 2-3x normal and shipping lines are not returning vessels to India, which may spill into Q2.
Timken-linked bearing ring export volumes continue to decline; recovery depends on new customer wins not yet visible.
Domestic auto components down 13% YoY on OEM production deferrals; Stellantis recovery is gradual.
Labour availability: recurrence of seasonal shortage and the cost of temporary labour.
Pending US duty drawback refunds: major chunk not yet received, so timing and size are uncertain.
Some US orders under the INR1.75 billion programme are on hold due to tariffs.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the order book but cautious on the near-term numbers: management openly attributed the revenue miss to labour and stated a conservative 21-22% margin guide due to freight. Answers on Timken, industrial bearings and the JV were more hedged and deferred to later quarters.
key_quotes: Though this looks short of our guided growth, our order book through the quarter was healthy, and the constraint we faced was not demand. It was an execution issue.
We are glad to report that the situation improved from June '26 onwards.

The EBITDA margin, what we have recorded, is 21.5% in this particular quarter, June '26*. We expect -- let me tell you conservatively, we expect that to be in the range of 21% to 22% in this fiscal FY27 conservatively.
Not INR500 crores, but I'm a bit confident to cross between INR425 crores to INR450 crores.
Yes, that would be added to revenue.

As we had flagged and informed previously also, we have not lost a single customer through the tariff disruption or even the war impact in European markets in the last year or even previous to last year.

adds.what: One or two new plants of a key export customer expected to start supply (customer's plants, not company-owned capacity)

growth.why: Mid-teen FY27 revenue growth guidance held, backed by healthy order book, export auto components guided to INR425-450 crore (vs INR350 crore FY26) and utilisation targeted up from 63-65% to 70-72%, though Q1 revenue grew only 4.3% and no company-owned capacity addition is quantified.
